title: The Richest Walk in the Gold Mine

concept.title: Empty a cell while you stand on it, and put the gold back when you leave
body: A mine is a grid of numbers: the gold in each cell. You may start in **any** cell that has gold, move up, down, left or right, collect the gold of every cell you enter, never enter a cell with no gold, and never visit a cell twice. Find the largest amount you can collect. This is a search over all roads, so use backtracking from every starting cell.

The grid itself serves as the "visited" table: a cell with 0 gold cannot be entered, so after taking the gold of a cell, the search cannot return to it. Restoring the value on the way back is the **unchoose** step. The function returns the best total **from this cell on**, so the best over all roads is found by taking the maximum.

statement: A gold mine is a grid with `r` rows and `c` columns; each cell has the amount of gold in it (it can be 0). You may start in any cell with gold. In one move you go to a neighbouring cell (above, below, left or right) that has gold. You collect all the gold of every cell you enter, and you never enter a cell twice. Print the largest amount of gold you can collect (0 if there is no gold).
inputFormat: Each of the next `r` lines has `c` integers.
outputFormat: Print the maximum amount of gold.

examples.note: The cell with 8 connects four dead ends, so a walk is a dead end, then 8, then another dead end. The best is 9 -> 8 -> 7 with 24.

hints: Try every cell with gold as the start.
Take the gold of the cell by setting it to 0, try the neighbours that still have gold, and restore the value.
Return the gold of the cell plus the best result of its neighbours.

solution.complexity: Time exponential in the number of cells (about 2 * 10^5 steps for 20 cells), space O(r * c).
